```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("../code"))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
from osim import natl_sim as ns

REPS = list(range(5))
PAR_LAB = {"phi": "Variance", "th_lon": "Zonal range", "th_lat": "Meridional range", "th_t": "Temporal range"}
LAYER_LAB = {"ohc_15_700": "15-700 m", "ohc_700_2000": "700-2000 m"}

def _emit(s=""):
    print(s)
    sys.stdout.flush()

def _show_fig(fig):
    display(fig)
    plt.close(fig)

def _tabs(items):
    _emit("::: {.panel-tabset}")
    for name, show in items:
        _emit(f"\n## {name}\n")
        show()
    _emit(":::")
```

Each replicate's float profiles are mapped as in Sukianto, Kuusela et al. (2026): the OHC of each layer
(15--700 m and 700--2000 m) minus the replicate's own local least-squares mean field is modelled, in each window, as a
zero-mean Gaussian process with the anisotropic exponential space-time covariance
$$
k\big((x,y,t),(x',y',t')\big) = \phi\,\exp\!\Big\{-\Big[\big(\tfrac{x-x'}{\theta_{\mathrm{lon}}}\big)^2
+ \big(\tfrac{y-y'}{\theta_{\mathrm{lat}}}\big)^2 + \big(\tfrac{t-t'}{\theta_t}\big)^2\Big]^{1/2}\Big\}
+ \sigma^2\,\mathbb{1}\{(x,y,t)=(x',y',t')\},
$$
with $x, y$ in degrees and $t$ in days. A window is a cell of the $2^\circ$ parameter grid and a season: the profiles
within $\pm 10^\circ$ of the cell centre and within $\pm 45$ days of the 15th of January, April, July or October, in each
year 2015--2025, the years being independent replicates with common parameters. Parameters are maximum-likelihood
estimates under the Vecchia approximation (GpGp, `exponential_scaledim`, 30 neighbours). A replicate's plug-in for a cell
is the median over its four seasonal fits; the pooled plug-in is the median over all twenty fits of the cell
(5 replicates $\times$ 4 seasons). The nugget-to-sill ratio $\sigma^2/\phi$ is negligible (median $1.7\times10^{-4}$ and $0.9\times10^{-4}$ over the window fits of the two layers) and is not shown.

A fit has run away when a range parameter leaves the bounds of a physically plausible window fit
($\theta_{\mathrm{lon}}, \theta_{\mathrm{lat}} \le 40^\circ$, $\theta_t \le 400$ days); such cells are left blank.
Ranges are fitted in degrees (as in Sukianto, Kuusela et al.) and mapped in km, $\theta_{\mathrm{lon}}\cdot\frac{\pi R}{180}\cos(\mathrm{lat})$ and $\theta_{\mathrm{lat}}\cdot\frac{\pi R}{180}$ with $R = 6371$ km at the cell-centre latitude, so that a correlation isotropic in distance shows equal zonal and meridional ranges. Each parameter has one colour scale across the six maps, spanning all values that did not run away.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Domain median of the plug-ins (ranges in km and days) per replicate and pooled; cv_between is the median over cells of the coefficient of variation of the five replicates' plug-ins; runaway counts replicate-cells left blank (of 5 x 733)."

t = ns.cov_summary(REPS)
t["layer"] = t.layer.map(LAYER_LAB)
t["parameter"] = t.parameter.map(PAR_LAB)
display(Markdown(t.round(3).to_markdown(index=False)))
```
